claims.text: HfNbTaTiZr is a refractory high-entropy alloy.
The alloy's high-temperature creep, cold-rolling hardness, and temperature-dependent modulus behavior share a common origin in thermally induced lattice distortions and residual stresses.
Microstructural precipitates can alter mechanical behavior in alloys from the HfNbTaTiZr system.
Precipitates and cold-work dislocation networks have thermal-expansion behavior different from that of the surrounding HfNbTaTiZr matrix.
Thermal-expansion mismatch between heterogeneous features and the matrix generates residual stresses during cooling or reheating.
Mismatch-induced residual stresses modulate dislocation mobility.
Mismatch-induced residual stresses alter interatomic spacing.
The proposed homogenized as-cast initial state has minimal microsegregation and low dislocation density.
Aging HfNbTaTiZr at 600–800 °C induces precipitate-bearing microstructural heterogeneity.
Cold rolling after aging produces a higher dislocation density.
Rapid annealing minimizes compositional segregation and microstructural heterogeneity in HfNbTaTiZr.
The proposed comparison varies only microstructural heterogeneity and its associated residual stresses.
Residual thermal stresses control high-temperature creep resistance in HfNbTaTiZr.
Residual thermal stresses govern the temperature dependence of the alloy's elastic modulus.
Residual thermal stresses contribute to the increased hardness produced by cold rolling.
Aged and cold-rolled samples will have higher diffraction-measured residual stress than homogenized samples.
Aged and cold-rolled samples will have higher yield strength than the homogenized baseline.
Aged and cold-rolled samples will have greater creep resistance at 1250 °C than the homogenized baseline.
Aged and cold-rolled samples will show elastic-modulus trends from 293 to 1100 K that deviate more strongly from a mixture rule than those of homogenized samples.
The proposed residual-stress mechanism operates from room temperature to 1250 °C and becomes especially evident after aging at 600–800 °C followed by cold work.

contradictions.description: The comparison is said to vary only heterogeneity and residual stress, but the aged arm is also cold rolled while the baseline is rapidly annealed. The arms therefore explicitly differ in dislocation density, precipitate population, aging history, and deformation history, so residual stress is not isolated as the sole governing variable.
